title: Meet the New Otterlike Predator That Scurried Alongside Dinosaurs - Nautilus
gist: An international team published in Nature a new, relatively large mammaliaform, Megacauda sungei, found in the collections of the Paleontological Museum of Liaoning but originating from a Mongolian fossil assemblage; the article frames its unique throat as a step toward mammals' big brains.

insights.claim: Paleontologists described a new and relatively large mammaliaform, Megacauda sungei, in the journal Nature.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Adds to evidence that early mammal relatives were more diverse in size than assumed.
insights.quote: After a thorough analysis they published their findings in Nature, naming the mammaliaform Megacauda sungei.

insights.claim: The Megacauda sungei specimen was discovered in the collections of the Paleontological Museum of Liaoning in Shenyang, China, though it originated from a fossil assemblage in Mongolia.

insights.so_what: Museum collections remain an underexploited source of new discoveries.

insights.claim: Many tiny protomammals lived alongside dinosaurs, a part of the ecosystem popular depictions like Jurassic Park omit.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Popular narratives skew perceptions of ancient ecosystems.
insights.quote: There were plenty of tiny protomammals scurrying around at the time, as well.

insights.claim: According to the article, the otterlike predator's unique throat anatomy paved the way for the evolution of large mammalian brains.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
